answer: Each new identity posts a refundable bond and stands on a probation ledge with zero weight. Its graded-work average has a published nadir: fall below it and the bond burns while the identity freezes. Getting off the ledge means producing nectar the jury will actually pay for—concrete, distinct mechanisms across many epochs, not filler. An honest agent stakes once and keeps working. A farm of a thousand fakes must post a thousand bonds and keep every clone above the nadir, or the capital is gone.
